summary: A note on two new features of the Multics network software. One is case mapping, activated by typing MAP, which helps users on upper-case-only terminals. It describes typing conventions for letters and some symbols. The other new feature is also described.

eli5.summary: A computer added a trick for people with keyboards that only type capital letters, so they can still use it properly.

subtitle: Case mapping and better allocation handling for Multics network users

tldr.problem: Users with upper-case-only terminals cannot easily access Multics, which expects lowercase input. Also, sending data to systems with small allocations causes frequent pauses and overhead.
tldr.mechanism: Case mapping translates uppercase to lowercase with special character codes for symbols. Interrupt-time code processes allocation messages without waking the daemon process.
tldr.outcome: Upper-case terminal users can work with Multics using special conventions. Network communication with allocation-limited systems becomes faster.

facts.label: Overhead reduction
facts.value: 75% of control-message time was for allocations

today: RFC 411 announced improvements to Multics network software in November 1972. Neither feature was superseded; they were operational improvements to the system.

sections.title: Two Improvements for Multics Network Users
sections.content: Multics network software has added two features to improve usability and performance. The first helps users on upper-case-only terminals access Multics through TIP (Terminal IMP, a network access device). The second speeds up data transfer to systems that offer small buffer allocations.
sections.eli5: Two changes make Multics easier to use: one helps special keyboards, and one makes sending files faster.

sections.title: Case Mapping for Limited Terminals
sections.content:
Typing MAP on an upper-case-only terminal activates software that applies typing conventions. Most alphabetic input is mapped to lowercase except after certain characters. Special symbols are typed using escape sequences: Control-H for backspace, and codes for grave accent, left brace, vertical bar, right brace, and tilde. The same conventions are already used for TENEX Model 33/35 TTYs, so they are familiar to some users. Typing HELP before login will also activate case mapping and display login instructions.

These escape sequences match existing Multics conventions for direct-dialed terminals.
sections.eli5: When you type MAP, Multics learns your keyboard only has capital letters and translates what you type into the lowercase it expects, using special codes for symbols you cannot type directly.

sections.title: Faster Data Transfer with Small Allocations
sections.content: Systems that offer small allocations (buffer space for incoming data) used to cause frequent pauses in output and wasted effort in the Multics Network Daemon process, which would wake up repeatedly to handle allocation messages (ALL control messages). The new scheme runs allocation-processing code at interrupt time, handling the messages and sending the next group of data without waking the daemon. Testing shows the improvement is significant. About 75% of network control-message processing time was spent on allocations, so this change substantially reduces overhead.
sections.eli5: When sending to computers with small buffers, the old way meant lots of interruptions. The new way handles those automatically so the system does not have to wake up so often.
